title: Acquired EGFR C797S mutation mediates resistance to AZD9291 in non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR T790M.
abstract: Here we studied cell-free plasma DNA (cfDNA) collected from subjects with advanced lung cancer whose tumors had developed resistance to the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) AZD9291.

We first performed next-generation sequencing of cfDNA from seven subjects and detected an acquired EGFR C797S mutation in one; expression of this mutant EGFR construct in a cell line rendered it resistant to AZD9291.
We then performed droplet digital PCR on serial cfDNA specimens collected from 15 AZD9291-treated subjects.

All were positive for the T790M mutation before treatment, but upon developing AZD9291 resistance three molecular subtypes emerged: six cases acquired the C797S mutation, five cases maintained the T790M mutation but did not acquire the C797S mutation and four cases lost the T790M mutation despite the presence of the underlying EGFR activating mutation.

Our findings provide insight into the diversity of mechanisms through which tumors acquire resistance to AZD9291 and highlight the need for therapies that are able to overcome resistance mediated by the EGFR C797S mutation.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: The AURA study (NCT01802632) is a phase I study of AZD9291 which enrolled subjects with EGFR-mutant lung cancer and acquired resistance to EGFR TKI to escalating doses of AZD9291 (20-240mg).

body.section: Trial design
body.text: At each dose level, expansion cohorts specifically studied patients with EGFR T790M+ or T790M- tumors based on a central genotyping assay.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: The study received IRB approval at all participating centers, and all patients provided informed consent prior to treatment.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: On this study, objective tumor response was assessed using the Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST).

body.section: Trial design
body.text: For the initial exploratory NGS cohort, we selected 7 subjects from the AURA trial (4 male, 3 female, median age 52, range 33-65) based upon availability of pretreatment and post-progression plasma specimens, regardless of evidence of sensitivity to therapy.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: We then performed the confirmatory plasma analysis on subjects meeting criteria for acquired resistance to AZD9291, defined as one scan demonstrating response or stable disease on imaging, followed by development of systemic progression on treatment.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: From this population, we only studied those with paired pretreatment and end-of-treatment plasma specimens available as of 9/22/2014.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: We further limited the analysis to subjects harboring EGFR L858R or exon 19 deletions, excluding subjects with rare activating mutations not detectable with existing ddPCR assays.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: We also omitted from the resistance analysis those subjects with no detectable L858R or exon 19 deletion in cfDNA at time of progression due to the probability of inadequate cfDNA shed to allow genomic studies to be performed.

body.section: Trial design
body.text: Nineteen subjects met these eligibility criteria and were included in the confirmatory plasma analysis (5 male, 14 female, median age 56, range 28-72).

body.section: Collection of plasma and extraction of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
body.text: Per the AURA study protocol, plasma was collected for all subjects on study when feasible to allow for genomic analysis of cfDNA.

body.section: Collection of plasma and extraction of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
body.text: 10-20 cc of blood were collected into EDTA tubes pretreatment, intermittently on treatment (dependent on the specific cohort), and again when coming off AZD9291.

body.section: Collection of plasma and extraction of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
body.text: In a parallel study at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI), we additionally consented subjects on the same clinical trial to collection of specimens every 3 weeks for more detailed analysis of response and progression kinetics.

body.section: Collection of plasma and extraction of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
body.text: Within 4 hours of collection, whole blood was centrifuged for 10 min at 1200g after which the plasma supernatant was further cleared by centrifugation for 10 min at 3000g.

body.section: Collection of plasma and extraction of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
body.text: Cleared plasma was stored in cryostat tubes at -80C until use.

body.section: Collection of plasma and extraction of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
body.text: Cell free DNA was isolated using the QIAmp Circulating Nucleic Acid Kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

body.section: Collection of plasma and extraction of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)
body.text: DNA was eluted in AVE buffer (100 uL) and stored at -80 °C.

body.section: NGS of plasma cfDNA
body.text: For plasma NGS, we PCR amplified all coding exons of a 20 gene panel using the Qiagen GeneRead Lung Cancer version 1 kit (catalog # 180941 NGHS-005Z-96); genes in this panel are listed in Supplementary Table 2.

body.section: NGS of plasma cfDNA
body.text: We prepared libraries of amplified DNA with the Kapa Hyperprep kit (catalog # KK8502).

body.section: NGS of plasma cfDNA
body.text: We then performed ultra-deep sequencing on an Illumina HiSeq instrument (2×100 bp) following QC with an Agilent TapeStation.

body.section: NGS of plasma cfDNA
body.text: We analyzed NGS data within the BCBio framework (https://bcbio-nextgen.readthedocs.org/en/latest/) using an AstraZeneca-developed variant calling algorithm (https://github.com/AstraZeneca-NGS/VarDict).

body.section: NGS of plasma cfDNA
body.text: NGS was performed once one on each specimen.

body.section: NGS of plasma cfDNA
body.text: Given the difficulty of accurate variant calling when using plasma-derived cfDNA and ultra-deep coverage of genes of interest (average 30,000×), we manually inspected variant calls of interest in IGV.

body.section: NGS of plasma cfDNA
body.text: We compared EGFR activating and resistance mutations to orthogonal genotyping data from plasma and tissue.

body.text: We introduced mutant EGFR constructs into authenticated Ba/F3 cells by retroviral infection as previously described,.

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: Parental Ba/F3 cell lines were obtained previously from the laboratory of James Griffin at DFCI.

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: We assessed growth and inhibition of growth by MTS assay performed according to previously established methods., We exposed mutant Ba/F3 cells to drug treatment for 72 hours and plotted the data relative to non-drug treated cells with the same genotype.

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: We set up all experimental points in six wells and repeated all experiments three times.

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: We graphically displayed the data using GraphPad Prism version 5.0 for Windows, (GraphPad Software; www.graphpad.com), fitting the curves using a non-linear regression model with a sigmoidal dose response.

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: Following drug treatment for 6 hours, we lysed Ba/F3 cells in NP-40 buffer (Cell Signaling Technology).

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: We conducted Western blot analyses after separation by SDS/PAGE electrophoresis and transfer to polyvinylidene difluoride-P membrane (Millipore).

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: We performed immunoblotting according to the antibody manufacturers’ recommendations and detected antibody binding using an enhanced chemiluminescence system (Perkin Elmer Inc.).

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: The phospho-specific EGFR (pY1068) antibody was purchased from Cell Signaling (#3777s).

body.section: C797S cell line studies
body.text: Total EGFR and Tubulin antibodies were purchased from Bethyl Laboratories (#A300-388A) and Sigma (#T9026), respectively.

body.section: Droplet digital PCR of plasma cfDNA
body.text: We developed EGFR C797S ddPCR assays in a similar fashion as previously described for other EGFR mutations.

body.section: Droplet digital PCR of plasma cfDNA
body.text: In brief, we custom designed primer and probe pairs, optimizing them for annealing temperature and cycling condition using serial dilutions of mutant DNA we obtained from Ba/F3 cells with and without EGFR T790M/C797S.

body.text: We ran each ddPCR assay in triplicate, each using 1/20th of the DNA isolated from 2mL plasma.

body.section: Droplet digital PCR of plasma cfDNA
body.text: We analyzed the results using QuantaSoft (ver 1.6.6) software that accompanied the QX100 reader.

body.section: Droplet digital PCR of plasma cfDNA
body.text: In our analyses, EGFR mutation specific signals are generated in the FAM channel while the EGFR wildtype signals are in the VIC channel.

body.section: Droplet digital PCR of plasma cfDNA
body.text: We dynamically determined cut-off values for positive signals using cell lysate controls with the respective EGFR mutations run concomitantly.

body.text: We calculated poisson concentrations using QuantaSoft, and EGFR mutation concentrations were adjusted to mL of plasma as follows: * 3.33. %mut were calculated from generated Poisson concentrations as follows: %mut=[FAM][FAM+VIC]∗100.

body.text: Serial ddPCR measurements were plotted from start of treatment with AZD9291 until time of systemic progression.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: We extracted DNA from 5×10 um sliced sections of FFPE material using the Maxwell FFPE Tissue LEV DNA Purification Kit.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: Tumor area content was evaluated by a clinical pathologist to confirm adequacy for sequencing; a minimum tumor content was set to 20%, in order to better detect somatic mutations.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: An initial multiplex-PCR with a proof-reading polymerase was performed on samples.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: For NGS, Vall d’Hebron Institute of Oncology has developed a panel of over 600 primer pairs targeting frequent mutations in oncogenes plus several tumor suppressors, totaling 57 genes, including EGFR; see Supplementary Table 2 for a list of genes included.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: We pooled indexed libraries and sequenced then on a MiSeq instrument (2×100) at an average coverage of 3000×.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: Initial alignment was performed with BWA after primer sequence clipping and variant calling was done with the GATK Unified Genotyper and VarScan2 followed by ANNOVAR annotation.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: Mutations were called at a minimum 3% allele frequency.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: SNPs were filtered out with dbSNP and 1000 genome datasets.

body.section: Next-generation sequencing of resistance tumor biopsies
body.text: All detected variants were manually checked.

supplements.caption: Supplementary Fig. 1: Acquired resistance to AZD9291. The index case (Subject #1) was treated with AZD9291 for advanced lung cancer harboring T790M, and had a partial response (-43%) after 6 weeks followed by systemic progression at 23 weeks.Supplementary Fig. 2: C797S mediates drug resistance in the absence of T790M. (a) Ba/F3 cells with different EGFR genotypes were treated with either AZD9291 or CO-1686 at the indicated concentrations, and viable cells were measured after 72 hours of treatment and plotted relative to untreated control cells. Experiments were repeated 3 times, with mean and standard deviation plotted at each concentration. The curves were fitted using a non-linear regression model with a sigmoidal dose response. (b) These same cells were treated with 1.0 μM AZD9291 or CO-1686 for 6 hours. Cell extracts were immunoblotted to detect the indicated proteins.Supplementary Fig. 3: Development of ddPCR assays for EGFR C797S. (a, b) Primer and probe pairs were custom designed and optimized for annealing temperature and cycling condition using serial dilutions of mutant DNA obtained from Ba/F3 cells with and without EGFR T790M/C797S.Supplementary Fig. 4: Technical sensitivity of ddPCR assays for EGFR C797S. (a-b, c-d) Similar to our previously developed ddPCR assays, the EGFR C797S ddPCR assays achieved a sensitivity between 0.05% and 0.1%.Supplementary Table 1: Plasma genotyping results at time of progression demonstrate three molecular subtypes of acquired resistance to AZD9291 in the 15 T790M+ cases. Acquired C797S was detected in 6 subjects (40%, blue), but was never detected at baseline. In 5 subjects (33%, orange), T790M is detected at progression without a resistance mechanism identified. Loss of the T790M mutation was seen in 4 subjects (27%, green), suggesting overgrowth of T790M- clones. Sens = TKI-sensitive EGFR mutation. ND= not detected. ULQ= upper limit of quantification.Supplementary Table 2: Genes included in the plasma and tumor next-generation sequencing (NGS) panels.
